title: R.F.K. Jr.’s Newest Mission: Getting Us Off Antidepressants

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半打电话给总统，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空度过七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天使用不同的起始词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，持续助您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 享受优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In his latest public health crusade, Robert F.
sentences.zh: 在他的最新公共卫生运动中，小罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy Jr.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪

sentences.en: is asking why millions of Americans have been taking psychiatric drugs for far longer than ever intended.
sentences.zh: 正在质问为什么数百万美国人服用精神类药物的时间远远超出了原本的预期。

sentences.en: I have been on Zoloft since I was eight years old.
sentences.zh: 我从八岁起就开始服用左洛复。

sentences.en: I've continuously been on antidepressants 27 years.
sentences.zh: 我连续服用抗抑郁药已经27年了。

sentences.en: I've been on Luvox 30 years.
sentences.zh: 我服用氟伏沙明已经30年了。

sentences.en: I've been on them longer than I've not been on them.
sentences.zh: 我吃药的时间比没吃药的时间还要长。

sentences.en: In the process, he's highlighting an open secret in medicine.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，他揭示了医学界一个公开的秘密。

sentences.en: That doctors are much better at starting drug treatments than at stopping them.
sentences.zh: 那就是医生们在开始药物治疗方面要比在停止治疗方面拿手得多。

sentences.en: I was told to take it daily and I never questioned that.
sentences.zh: 我被告知要每天服用，而我从未对此产生过怀疑。

sentences.en: I don't really think I even asked or thought about how long I would be on it.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为我甚至没有问过或想过我会吃多久。

sentences.en: I did not know that I was going to be on him for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道自己余生都要靠它。

sentences.en: And that patients who want to end their treatment are increasingly taking matters into their own hands.
sentences.zh: 而那些希望结束治疗的患者正越来越多地自己采取行动。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, I felt so strongly that my brain was like, you need to get off this medication.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我强烈地感觉到我的大脑在说，你需要停掉这种药物。

sentences.en: Today, Ellen Berry takes us inside the growing movement to deprescribe.
sentences.zh: 今天，埃伦·贝里带我们深入了解日益壮大的“减药停药”运动。

sentences.en: It's Monday, June 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月22日，星期一。

sentences.en: Nice to have you on the show.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Let me just start by asking how you came to this topic of deprescribing.
sentences.zh: 我想先问问你是怎么接触到减药停药这个话题的。

sentences.en: And for the uninitiated, can you just define that phrase?
sentences.zh: 对于外行人来说，你能简单定义一下这个词吗？

sentences.en: Deprescribing is the art and science of carefully tapering off a psychiatric medication or reducing a psychiatric medication.
sentences.zh: 减药停药是一门艺术与科学，指谨慎地逐渐减少精神类药物的用量或缩减精神类药物。

sentences.en: I first heard the term really from patient groups.
sentences.zh: 我最初确实是从患者群体中听到这个词的。

sentences.en: There has long been a sort of a subculture of people who talk to each other on the Internet about being harmed by medication
sentences.zh: 长期以来存在着一种亚文化群体，人们在互联网上交流因药物而受到的伤害，

sentences.en: or feeling that their medication isn't working anymore, who sort of compare notes on how to get off them.
sentences.zh: 或者觉得他们的药物不再起作用了，他们互相交流如何戒掉这些药物的心得。

sentences.en: And those communities, that's nothing new.
sentences.zh: 而这些社群，并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: They've been out there for decades, really, since the early days of social media.
sentences.zh: 它们其实已经存在了几十年，从社交媒体的早期就开始了。

sentences.en: But what's new is that this group, largely of patients, now has a seat at the table as federal health policy is developed.
sentences.zh: 但新鲜的是，这个主要由患者组成的群体，现在在制定联邦卫生政策时有了发言权。

sentences.en: And that's because of RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 而这全拜小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪所赐。

sentences.en: I want to thank President Trump for entrusting me to deliver on his promise to make America healthy again.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢特朗普总统信任我，让我兑现他让美国再次健康的承诺。

sentences.en: Secretary Kennedy made it clear during his confirmation hearings that one of the things he was looking at would be curbing the use of psychiatric medications in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪部长在听证会上明确表示，他正在关注的事情之一就是遏制美国精神类药物的使用。

sentences.en: 15 percent of American youth are now on Adderall or some other ADHD medication.
sentences.zh: 15%的美国青少年现在正在服用阿得拉或其他多动症药物。

sentences.en: He talked specifically about antidepressants in those hearings, that these medications were sort of dependence-forming, that we prescribe them to freely.
sentences.zh: 他在听证会上特别谈到了抗抑郁药，认为这些药物容易让人产生依赖，我们开处方开得太随意了。

sentences.en: Even higher percentages are on SSRIs and benzos.
sentences.zh: 更高比例的人在使用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂和苯二氮卓类药物。

sentences.en: We are not just over-medicating our children.
sentences.zh: 我们不只是在给孩子们过度用药。

sentences.en: We're over-medicating our entire population.
sentences.zh: 我们在给整个人口过度用药。

sentences.en: And what he was talking about was the most widely used category of psychiatric medications, SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 而他所谈论的是使用最广泛的精神类药物类别，即选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂。

sentences.en: Listen, I know people, including members of my family, who've had a much worse time getting off of SSRIs than people that have getting off of heroin.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认识一些人，包括我的家庭成员，他们戒掉选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂比戒掉海洛因还要痛苦得多。

sentences.en: He said that SSRI antidepressants are harder to quit than heroin.
sentences.zh: 他说，选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂类抗抑郁药比海洛因更难戒掉。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: No, there's no evidence supporting that.
sentences.zh: 不，没有任何证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: SSRIs are used by probably around 35 million American adults.
sentences.zh: 大约有3500万美国成年人使用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂。

sentences.en: These are selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors like Prozac or Zoloft or Lexapro.
sentences.zh: 这些是选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂，比如百忧解、左洛复或来士普。

sentences.en: They're considered so safe to prescribe that overwhelmingly they're prescribed by family doctors or GPs rather than psychiatrists.
sentences.zh: 它们被认为非常安全，以至于绝大多数情况下是由家庭医生或全科医生而不是精神科医生开具处方。

sentences.en: And they're used for sort of an ever-expanding array of different problems, not just for depression, but also for all kinds of anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder,
sentences.zh: 它们用于不断扩大的各种问题，不仅用于治疗抑郁症，还用于治疗各种焦虑症、强迫症、

sentences.en: social anxiety, PTSD.
sentences.zh: 社交焦虑、创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: And that list, you know, has just continued to get longer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个清单一直在变长。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And here he is assailing and questioning the most widely used medication in basically all of mental health.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，他正在抨击和质疑几乎整个心理健康领域使用最广泛的药物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So after the confirmation hearings at the beginning of 2025, I think we were all watching closely to see what was he actually planning to do.
sentences.zh: 所以在2025年初的听证会之后，我想我们都在密切关注他到底打算做什么。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of May, Secretary Kennedy appeared at a summit on over-medicalization that was held by the Maha Institute and Intercompass Initiative,
sentences.zh: 在5月初，肯尼迪部长出席了由马哈研究所和互通倡议组织举办的关于过度医疗化的峰会，

sentences.en: which is a support organization for people going off mental health medications.
sentences.zh: 这是一个为戒掉心理健康药物的人提供支持的组织。

sentences.en: The thesis of the entire day was overuse of SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 整场会议的核心论点就是过度使用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂。

sentences.en: And at the end of that day, he announced a set of regulatory changes that all kind of aimed to encourage clinicians to help patients get off SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 在那天结束时，他宣布了一系列监管变革，旨在鼓励临床医生帮助患者停用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So he's beginning to articulate a kind of federal regulatory vision for deprescription.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始阐述一种针对减药停药的联邦监管愿景。

sentences.en: What specifically is he proposing?
sentences.zh: 他具体提出了什么？

sentences.en: He sent a Dear Colleague letter, which is direct communication to hospitals and doctors.
sentences.zh: 他发出了一封致同仁信，这是与医院和医生的直接沟通。

sentences.en: And the Dear Colleague letter essentially said, don't default to using medication for depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 这封致同仁信基本上说的是，不要默认对抑郁和焦虑使用药物治疗。

sentences.en: Look at other modes of treatment.
sentences.zh: 看看其他的治疗方式。

sentences.en: And we know that lots of things are effective treatments for depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们知道有很多方法是治疗抑郁和焦虑的有效手段。

sentences.en: Psychotherapy is probably the number one alternate mode, but also sleep and exercise and diet and lots of other things.
sentences.zh: 心理治疗可能是首选的替代模式，还有睡眠、运动、饮食以及许多其他事情。

sentences.en: So that is sort of common sense advice.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一种常识性的建议。

sentences.en: It wasn't controversial.
sentences.zh: 它并不具争议性。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, he's not a doctor, RFK Jr., but he's basically writing a letter to colleagues in the world of public health and the medical community.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪不是医生，但他基本上是在给公共卫生界和医疗界的同仁写信。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then he introduced a billing code that would allow Medicare and Medicaid providers to be reimbursed for helping patients get off medications.
sentences.zh: 接着他引入了一项计费代码，允许医疗保险和医疗补助服务提供者因帮助患者停药而获得报销。

sentences.en: And why is that important?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: It's important because it can be complicated and time consuming to help people quit a psychiatric medication,
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为帮助人们戒掉精神类药物可能很复杂且耗时，

sentences.en: especially if they've been taking it for a long time or they're taking a complicated cocktail of four or five psychiatric medications.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果他们已经服用很长时间，或者正在服用由四、五种精神类药物组成的复杂鸡尾酒疗法。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of time and usually psychiatrists are reimbursed for 15-minute med checks every month.
sentences.zh: 这需要大量时间，通常精神科医生每个月因15分钟的用药检查获得报销。

sentences.en: That's just not enough time.
sentences.zh: 这时间根本不够。

sentences.en: So he's financially attempting to incentivize doctors to participate in de-prescribing.
sentences.zh: 所以他试图在经济上激励医生参与减药停药。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And another thing he set in motion is what's called a technical expert panel to develop guidelines for tapering off SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 他启动的另一件事是所谓的专家技术小组，来制定逐步戒断选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂的指南。

sentences.en: And this panel would create a new set of recommendations for health care providers on how best to do this.
sentences.zh: 这个小组将为医疗保健提供者制定一套关于如何最好地做到这一点的新建议。

sentences.en: Ellen, what's the reaction to these proposals, to this speech from the Secretary of Health and Human Services from the world of medical experts out there?
sentences.zh: 埃伦，面对卫生与公众服务部长的这些提案和讲话，外界医疗专家的反应如何？

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 对，

sentences.en: I was really curious about that because it was noticeable that there were no medical organizations involved in putting together this sort of day of policymaking around the use of SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 我对此非常好奇，因为值得注意的是，在围绕选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂使用制定政策的这一天里，没有任何医疗组织参与其中。

sentences.en: And when I reached out to them, I think there was a degree of alarm that they had somehow been excluded from this process, which sort of drives it, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我联系他们时，我认为他们某种程度上感到惊慌，因为他们不知何故被排斥在这个过程之外，而这在某种程度上推动了

sentences.en: one of the central functions of psychiatry.
sentences.zh: 精神病学的一项核心功能。

sentences.en: And I had an opportunity to find out a little bit more about that because the American Psychiatric Association held its annual meeting 10 days later.
sentences.zh: 我有一个机会对此了解更多，因为美国精神医学学会10天后召开了年会上。

sentences.en: That is extremely convenient.
sentences.zh: 那真是太巧了。

sentences.en: Journalistically, I'm going to assume you went.
sentences.zh: 从新闻角度来看，我猜你去了。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: What I found was kind of twofold.
sentences.zh: 我发现的情况主要有两个方面。

sentences.en: Some people that I talked to were worried that this was just the first step in a much more ambitious plan on the side of Secretary Kennedy that would lead to a bigger discrediting of psychiatric treatments.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的一些人担心，这只是肯尼迪部长一项更雄心勃勃计划的第一步，这将导致对精神科治疗的更大程度的不信任。

sentences.en: So their fear is that whatever this is, it's just the beginning, maybe a side door into greater government, what, perhaps restrictions on these drugs?
sentences.zh: 所以他们的恐惧是，无论这是什么，这只是开始，也许是政府对这些药物实施更大程度的，怎么说呢，或许是限制的侧门？

sentences.en: So a lot of doctors who I interviewed in the hallways outside sessions at the APA said that SSRIs are the foundation of their practice, that they are so safe,
sentences.zh: 因此，我在APA会议场外走廊采访的许多医生都表示，选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂是他们执业的基础，它们非常安全，

sentences.en: that they've been using them for so many years, and that they turn people's lives around.
sentences.zh: 他们已经使用了很多年，并且它们彻底改变了人们的生活。

sentences.en: They make the difference between being able to get up in the morning and get dressed and get to work and not being able to do those things.
sentences.zh: 它们让人们在能够早起、穿衣、去上班和无法做到这些事情之间产生了区别。

sentences.en: So a lot of them were kind of passionate about saying what they have seen with patients.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很多人都满腔热情地讲述他们从患者身上看到的情况。

sentences.en: And I think the worry is that people are going to be driven away from taking medications or that somehow their access will be restricted.
sentences.zh: 我认为大家的担心是，人们会被吓得不敢吃药，或者他们的获取途径会以某种方式受到限制。

sentences.en: How many doctors at this conference were open to or even in agreement with what RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 这次会议上有多少医生对小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪在这里谈到的关于减药停药的内容

sentences.en: is talking about here when it comes to deprescription?
sentences.zh: 持开放态度甚至表示赞同？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there was a second big takeaway that I had from this gathering, which is that a substantial number of doctors there agreed that this is an area where we could do a lot better.
sentences.zh: 所以我有从这次聚会中获得的第二个重大收获，那就是那里的相当一部分医生一致认为，这是一个我们可以做得更好的领域。

sentences.en: That is, training of psychiatrists focuses a great deal on putting people on medications, but much less on what it means to take them off and what a challenge it can be.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，精神科医生的培训主要集中在让人吃药上，而对如何停药意味着什么以及这会带来多大挑战的关注则要少得多。

sentences.en: And a number of people I interviewed expressed frustration over that.
sentences.zh: 我采访的许多人对此表达了沮丧。

sentences.en: In one of the panels that I attended, a doctor, Ronald Winchell from Columbia University School of Medicine, said that when he looked back at his long career,
sentences.zh: 在我参加的一个小组讨论中，来自哥伦比亚大学医学院的医生罗纳德·温切尔表示，当他回顾自己漫长的职业生涯时，

sentences.en: one of the things that he most regretted is not taking patients off medications until later than he should have.
sentences.zh: 他最后悔的事情之一就是没有更早地让患者停药，直到拖得比应该停药的时间还要晚。

sentences.en: That is, that is, hesitating for various reasons, even when he thought that the medication was no longer needed or no longer effective.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，由于各种原因犹豫不决，即使在他认为不再需要或不再有效的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: It sounds like the second group of doctors you're talking to feel like RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 听起来你交谈的第二组医生觉得小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪

sentences.en: has identified a problem in their world that everyone should be more focused on.
sentences.zh: 指出了他们领域中每个人都应该更加关注的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there was a lot of discussion of deprescribing at this conference.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这次会议上有很多关于减药停药的讨论。

sentences.en: There was a number of panels on deprescribing different classes of medications.
sentences.zh: 有许多关于不同类别药物减药停药的小组讨论。

sentences.en: There was a new deprescribing handbook, and it was selling a lot downstairs in the exhibition hall.
sentences.zh: 有一本新的减药停药手册，在楼下的展厅里卖得很好。

sentences.en: And in conversations with doctors, a number of them acknowledged that this is an area where we could do a lot better at supporting patients.
sentences.zh: 在与医生的对话中，许多人承认这是一个我们在支持患者方面可以做得更好的领域。

sentences.en: One thing we haven't talked about here is objective research that would clarify the questions we're discussing.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里还没有讨论的一点是能够澄清我们正在讨论的问题的客观研究。

sentences.en: If, Ellen, the assumption now is that doctors aren't talking enough about getting off these drugs, that's certainly the case RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，如果现在的假设是医生对戒掉这些药物谈论得不够，这当然是小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪提出的观点，

sentences.en: is making, some doctors are making it too.
sentences.zh: 一些医生也这样认为。

sentences.en: The implication is that people are on these drugs for too long.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人们吃这些药的时间太长了。

sentences.en: So what does the research tell us about long-term use of SSRIs?
sentences.zh: 那么研究告诉我们关于长期使用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂的情况是什么？

sentences.en: The reality is that there isn't all that much research on that.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，并没有那么多关于这方面的研究。

sentences.en: Most of the clinical trials we have on these drugs are efficacy trials, and they're shorter term, like six- to eight-week trials that are necessary for FDA approval.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的关于这些药物的大多数临床试验都是疗效试验，而且时间较短，比如FDA批准所需的六到八周试验。

sentences.en: There's some longer-term work, but very little that tells us what happens after three years or five years or ten years.
sentences.zh: 有一些长期研究，但很少有告诉我们三年、五年或十年后会发生什么。

sentences.en: And I think when SSRIs were first introduced in the 1980s, it wasn't anticipated that people would be taking them for years and years.
sentences.zh: 我认为当选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂在20世纪80年代首次推出时，人们并没有预料到会连续吃上好几年。

sentences.en: The clinical guidelines say once someone's symptoms are in remission, that you should discontinue the medication after six, nine, 12 months and just go back off.
sentences.zh: 临床指南规定，一旦某个人的症状缓解，应该在六、九、十二个月后停药，然后停用。

sentences.en: But I think we see in reality that for a lot of people, that's just not happening.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们在现实中看到，对许多人来说，情况根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: So one study found that the median duration of treatment with an SSRI is five years.
sentences.zh: 因此一项研究发现，使用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂治疗的持续时间中位数是五年。

sentences.en: And for many, it's a lot longer than that.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，时间要长得多。

sentences.en: That amazes me, to be honest, that we don't have much of any long-term research on what has become for so many people long-term treatments.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这让我感到惊讶，对于已经成为许多人长期治疗手段的药物，我们居然几乎没有任何长期研究。

sentences.en: I mean, if millions and millions of people are taking these prescription drugs for years and years and years,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果有数以百万计的人年复一年地服用这些处方药，

sentences.en: it's deeply surprising that we don't know clinically what the impact of that is.
sentences.zh: 我们居然在临床上不知道这会产生什么影响，这让人感到深深的惊讶。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That kind of research just hasn't been a priority.
sentences.zh: 那种研究根本没有被列为优先事项。

sentences.en: So in the weeks since RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 所以在小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪提出这些想法后的几周里，一旦医学健康界开始吸收这些想法，这些提案究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: introduced these ideas and once the medical health world began to absorb them, what has actually happened to these proposals?
sentences.zh: 嗯，APA的新任主席将在一个专家技术小组中占有一席之地，该小组将制定这方面的指南。

sentences.en: Well, the incoming president of the APA is going to have a seat on one of the technical expert panels that will be developing guidelines in this area.
sentences.zh: 还有来自美国临床精神药理学学会的精神科医生。

sentences.en: There's also a psychiatrist from the American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology.
sentences.zh: 因此，主要专业集团的代表将参与其中。

sentences.en: So there are going to be representatives of sort of major professional groups at the table.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 所以许多医疗专家决定，即使他们对小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的议程持怀疑态度，他们也希望参与其中。

sentences.en: So a lot of these medical experts decided that even if they were skeptical of RFK Jr.'s agenda here, that they wanted to be a part of it.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you can't beat them, join them, shape them.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法打败他们，就加入他们，然后塑造他们。

sentences.en: They wanted a seat at the table.
sentences.zh: 他们想要在谈判桌上占有一席之地。

sentences.en: I mean, as this deprescribing project gets off the ground, it's involving both establishment mainstream psychiatry and across the table,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，随着这个减药项目的推进，它既涉及主流精神医学界，

sentences.en: representatives of a totally different group that has been watching psychiatry critically from the outside for a long time.
sentences.zh: 也涉及一个长期从外部批判性地关注精神医学的完全不同的代表群体。

sentences.en: And that includes patients who are saying, how long are we supposed to be on these things?
sentences.zh: 其中包括那些一直在问“我们到底还要吃这些药多久”的患者。

sentences.en: And why haven't we been having these conversations with our doctors the whole time?
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们没有从一开始就跟医生进行这些对话？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏部门拼字游戏“Connections”的创作者之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天都制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游戏。

sentences.en: Ellen, I want to turn to this world of patients who have been eager for this deprescription conversation to reach the point that it now has,
sentences.zh: 埃伦，我想谈谈这样一群患者：他们一直渴望关于减药的讨论能够发展到如今的阶段，

sentences.en: where the federal government is broaching it and medical experts are now joining the conversation.
sentences.zh: 也就是联邦政府开始探讨这一话题，医学专家也开始加入讨论。

sentences.en: And in particular, I want to better understand the specific reasons that patients are giving for wanting to get off these medications
sentences.zh: 特别是，我想更好地了解患者想要停用这些药物的具体原因，

sentences.en: and the specific experiences that lead them to that decision.
sentences.zh: 以及导致他们做出这一决定的具体经历。

sentences.en: Well, you know, whenever I write about this subject, we really get inundated with personal stories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，每当我写这个主题时，我们真的会收到大量个人的故事。

sentences.en: And people have different reasons for wanting to get off a medication.
sentences.zh: 人们想要停药的原因各不相同。

sentences.en: So I just thought, like, if I get off the depressions, I can see what life is without this numbness.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就想，如果我停掉抗抑郁药，我就能看看没有这种麻木感的生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: Sometimes they feel like their emotions have been kind of muffled.
sentences.zh: 有时候他们觉得自己的情绪被某种程度地压抑了。

sentences.en: I wasn't having these anxious thoughts, but I also wasn't experiencing, like, as much high good emotions either.
sentences.zh: 我没有了那些焦虑的想法，但我也同样体验不到那么多强烈的美好情绪了。

sentences.en: There was, like, delayed sexual side effects.
sentences.zh: 还出现了一些延迟的性副作用。

sentences.en: Sometimes they have side effects.
sentences.zh: 有时候他们会有副作用。

sentences.en: Sometimes they feel that the medication just isn't working anymore.
sentences.zh: 有时候他们觉得药物已经不管用了。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the classic thing.
sentences.zh: 也许这是经典的情况。

sentences.en: Oh, I feel great.
sentences.zh: 哦，我感觉好极了。

sentences.en: I must not need my medication anymore.
sentences.zh: 我一定不需要再吃药了。

sentences.en: By then, I had been on the medication for about 25 years.
sentences.zh: 到那时，我吃这种药大约有25年了。

sentences.en: And I was just curious, what would my life be like without this?
sentences.zh: 我只是很好奇，没有了它，我的生活会是什么样的？

sentences.en: And I've heard from a lot of people who said, you know, I started taking this medication when I was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 我听许多人说过，你知道，我十几岁时就开始吃这种药了。

sentences.en: And maybe that's what I needed to get through that period.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是我度过那个时期所需要的。

sentences.en: But now many years have passed and I've entered adulthood not exactly knowing who I was.
sentences.zh: 但现在很多年过去了，我步入了成年，却并不太清楚自己究竟是谁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who you would be without those drugs.
sentences.zh: 没有了那些药物，你会变成什么样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It's FOMO.
sentences.zh: 这就是错失恐惧症。

sentences.en: It's like, what am I missing out on?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我错过了什么？

sentences.en: I want to live in real life.
sentences.zh: 我想生活在现实生活中。

sentences.en: I don't want to live in black and white.
sentences.zh: 我不想生活在黑白世界里。

sentences.en: I want to live in color, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想生活在多姿多彩的世界里，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like, those intense emotions that can feel so uncomfortable, especially when you're a very young person, they're also part of your personality.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些可能会让人感到非常不适的强烈情绪，特别是当你还很年轻的时候，它们也是你个性的一部分。

sentences.en: And I hear from people who say, like, I want to know who that person is.
sentences.zh: 我听到有人说，我想知道那个真正的人是谁。

sentences.en: Once these people you're hearing from decide that they're going to try to stop taking these medications, how have they actually technically been doing that?
sentences.zh: 一旦你听说的这些人决定尝试停药，他们在技术上实际上是如何做到的？

sentences.en: And who is guiding them through that process?
sentences.zh: 又是谁在指导他们完成这个过程？

sentences.en: I mean, I think some people work with their doctors in getting off or tapering a medication and some people don't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为有些人会在医生的配合下停药或逐渐减量，而有些人则没有。

sentences.en: I went in and they were like, hey, you want a refill of your Zoloft?
sentences.zh: 我走进去，他们就问：嘿，你要续配左洛复吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, yes, I guess if I still need to be on it.
sentences.zh: 我说：好啊，如果我还需要吃的话。

sentences.en: And they were like, cool.
sentences.zh: 他们就说：行。

sentences.en: A lot of the people we hear from say this conversation about how to get off isn't happening with their doctor or if it is happening, it isn't satisfying.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的很多人都说，关于如何停药的讨论并没有与他们的医生进行，或者即使进行了，也并不能让人满意。

sentences.en: Or for others, they just don't see their doctor often enough to get the kind of robust support that they need.
sentences.zh: 或者对其他人来说，他们看医生的频率不够，无法获得他们所需的有力支持。

sentences.en: I'm not going to see all doctors, but I don't know if how many doctors really grasp what it is to be on an antidepressant.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说所有医生都这样，但我不知道到底有多少医生真正理解服用抗抑郁药是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Like if you go in there and you're feeling depressed, they say, all right, then you just raise the medication.
sentences.zh: 比如你走进去说你感到沮丧，他们就会说：好吧，那你把药量加大就行了。

sentences.en: Some are better than others, but I never really go to them to get off.
sentences.zh: 有些医生比别的医生好，但我从来不是为了停药去找他们的。

sentences.en: I did that myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己干的。

sentences.en: And in some cases, people just lose trust in their doctor if they think that the medication that they've been prescribed is making them worse.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，如果人们认为给自己开的药让病情加重了，他们就会对医生失去信任。

sentences.en: I'll be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: I, at this point, because I've been dismissed about everything else, I was like, I don't trust these people.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，因为我在其他所有事情上的意见都被忽视了，所以我想：我不信任这些人。

sentences.en: I can make my own health decisions.
sentences.zh: 我自己能做出健康决定。

sentences.en: And those people have been talking to each other now for years and years with a lot of frustration towards organized medicine.
sentences.zh: 这些人多年来一直在互相交流，对有组织的医疗体系积聚了大量的沮丧情绪。

sentences.en: And for those folks who have been trying to do this essentially DIY, what has been their playbook, for lack of a better word?
sentences.zh: 对于那些基本上在进行DIY（自行操作）的人来说，他们的“攻略”——如果可以这样称呼的话——是什么样的？

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 它看起来是怎样的？

sentences.en: I use Dr. Google and I look at forums on Reddit and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我用谷歌医生，看红迪网之类的论坛。

sentences.en: And people are like, if you do cold turkey, it can really destabilize you a little bit.
sentences.zh: 人们会说，如果你突然彻底停药，真的会让你有点心态失衡。

sentences.en: So the kind of subculture around tapering and withdrawing from medications has been out there since the early days of social media.
sentences.zh: 因此，围绕药物减量和戒断的亚文化在社交媒体的早期就已经存在了。

sentences.en: One example is a site called Surviving Antidepressants.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是一个叫做“摆脱抗抑郁药”的网站。

sentences.en: And what you would find there is people exchanging their withdrawal protocols, and it got incredibly technical.
sentences.zh: 你在那里会发现人们在交流他们的戒断方案，而且变得非常专业细致。

sentences.en: People would be talking about reducing their dosage by a single bead within the capsule or liquefying it or using pharmaceutical scales.
sentences.zh: 人们会讨论将剂量减少胶囊中的单一颗粒、将其液化或使用药用天平。

sentences.en: And over time, you know, that network has sort of matured into a real marketplace of support.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你知道，这个网络已经演变成了一个真正的互助市场。

sentences.en: And that's presumably to avoid the side effects of abruptly taking yourself off of one of these drugs.
sentences.zh: 这大概是为了避免突然停用其中一种药物所带来的副作用。

sentences.en: But even when people are very careful and very gradual, what are the side effects of ending these treatments?
sentences.zh: 但即便人们非常小心、非常循序渐进，结束这些治疗的副作用又是什么呢？

sentences.en: The side effects that you most often hear about are vertigo, nausea, or flu-like symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 你最常听到的副作用是眩晕、恶心或类似流感的症状。

sentences.en: I completely stopped sleeping.
sentences.zh: 我彻底失眠了。

sentences.en: Insomnia, something that they call brain zaps.
sentences.zh: 失眠，还有一种他们称之为“大脑电击感”的东西。

sentences.en: Electricity in my head.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里有电流感。

sentences.en: Which are like a twinge or a sense of a feeling of a sort of a shock-like sensation in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这就像是脑部的一种刺痛感，或者是一种类似触电的感觉。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's like this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就像是这种感觉。

sentences.en: And there's some portion of people who describe the process of withdrawal as really intolerable, like jumping out of their skin.
sentences.zh: 有一部分人形容戒断过程简直难以忍受，就像要跳出自己的皮囊一样。

sentences.en: And it is its own kind of debilitating crisis.
sentences.zh: 它本身就是一种使人衰弱的危机。

sentences.en: I would like watch a movie and cry.
sentences.zh: 我会看电影然后哭泣。

sentences.en: I'd watch a commercial and cry.
sentences.zh: 我会看广告然后哭泣。

sentences.en: Read a book and I'd cry.
sentences.zh: 读一本书我也会哭。

sentences.en: I was listening to the Beach Boys Pet Sounds album and just hear it's coming down my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我在听海滩男孩的《Pet Sounds》专辑，眼泪就止不住地往下流。

sentences.en: It felt good for a while, but then it was like having emotions that were like a dripping faucet to like a fire hose.
sentences.zh: 一开始感觉挺好，但后来情绪就像从滴水的水龙头变成了消防水龙带。

sentences.en: It was too much.
sentences.zh: 实在太多了。

sentences.en: But what doctors generally say is that for most people, these symptoms really only last for a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 但医生通常的说法是，对大多数人来说，这些症状其实只持续几周。

sentences.en: And then if after that you're feeling dramatic mood changes, you might be experiencing relapse.
sentences.zh: 如果在此之后你仍然感到剧烈的情绪波动，你可能正在经历复发。

sentences.en: Essentially, the conditions that may have prompted you to first go on these drugs.
sentences.zh: 本质上，就是最初促使你开始服用这些药物的那些状况。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: However severe these side effects are, they would seem to buttress the argument that the best version of deprescription is a medically supervised one.
sentences.zh: 无论这些副作用有多严重，它们似乎都在支持这样一种观点：最好版本的减药过程应该是经过医学监督的。

sentences.en: Where you're not trying to do it yourself and you're not determining dosages and tapering.
sentences.zh: 也就是你不是在自己瞎折腾，不是在自己决定剂量和减量方案。

sentences.en: And where the same doctor who prescribed the drug is the one helping you get off of them and aware that you're trying to do it and helping you manage what could be a brain zap or a resumption of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 而且开药的同一个医生在帮助你停药，并且知道你在这样做，还能帮你应对可能出现的大脑电击感或症状复发。

sentences.en: This feels like something that should not be DIY.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就不应该靠自己DIY。

sentences.en: That's certainly the view from within medicine that one of the reasons that you need supervision if you're doing something like this is just to guard against the possibility of a relapse.
sentences.zh: 医学界内部显然也是这种观点：如果你要做这样的事情，需要监督的原因之一就是为了防范复发的可能性。

sentences.en: And this would seem to make the case for the conversation that RFK is pushing the medical world to have.
sentences.zh: 这似乎也为小肯尼迪正在推动医学界进行的这场对话提供了理由。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think there is some acknowledgement that prescribers aren't putting the same amount of care and attention into landing the plane as taking off.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们已经有了一些共识，即处方医生在停药（让飞机降落）时投入的关怀和注意力，并没有起飞时那么多。

sentences.en: Well, Ellen, here I want to acknowledge that the conversation that RFK is trying to have and that we're having here is not theoretical for me anyway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，埃伦，在这里我要承认，小肯尼迪试图发起的以及我们现在正在进行的这场对话，对我来说无论如何都不是理论上的。

sentences.en: And here I'm going to shake my Lexapro.
sentences.zh: 在这里我要摇晃一下我的来士普药瓶。

sentences.en: I've been on Lexapro as an anti-anxiety medication for at least a decade.
sentences.zh: 我作为抗焦虑药物服用来士普至少有十年了。

sentences.en: It was prescribed by a psychiatrist, but then just became part of my relationship with my general practitioner.
sentences.zh: 它是由精神科医生开具的，但后来就成了我和全科医生诊疗关系的一部分。

sentences.en: I just kind of get it renewed.
sentences.zh: 我只是去续药。

sentences.en: And I've not really been asked to think about how long I should be on it.
sentences.zh: 没有人真正要求我去思考我到底应该吃多久。

sentences.en: And now suddenly having this conversation with you is making me ask that question.
sentences.zh: 而现在突然和你进行这场对话，让我开始问自己这个问题。

sentences.en: How long am I supposed to be on it?
sentences.zh: 我到底应该吃多久？

sentences.en: What would happen if I stopped taking it?
sentences.zh: 如果我停药会发生什么？

sentences.en: Would all the white noise of anxiety that made me want to go on Lexapro, would that return?
sentences.zh: 当初让我想要服用来士普的所有焦虑杂音，会卷土重来吗？

sentences.en: Or 10 years later, have I outgrown that and I just don't know it because I've never tried to taper myself off this to find out who I would be if I weren't me on Lexapro?
sentences.zh: 还是说十年后，我已经不再需要它了，只是我自己不知道，因为我从来没有尝试过自己减药来看看，如果我不是吃着来士普的那个我，我会是谁？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not a simple question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: I hear so many people asking that kind of question.
sentences.zh: 我听到很多人都在问这种问题。

sentences.en: Like, is there some authentic self that I want to go back to?
sentences.zh: 比如，是否存在某个我想回去的真实的自我？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, what would life look like if I took this medication away?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我把这种药物拿掉，生活会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I just think that question is percolating.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这个问题正在酝酿发酵。

sentences.en: And I feel like what's a little bit more complicated is if you think it works for you, you become sort of, I don't know, psychologically attached to them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得更复杂的是，如果你认为它对你有用，你就会对它们产生某种，我不知道，心理上的依赖。

sentences.en: And you think, if I quit this, am I going to spiral?
sentences.zh: 你会想，如果我戒了，我的状态会失控吗？

sentences.en: Am I going to feel bad again?
sentences.zh: 我会再次感觉糟糕吗？

sentences.en: And we know that the placebo effect is a huge part of the picture with these medications.
sentences.zh: 我们知道安慰剂效应在这些药物的作用中占据了很大一部分。

sentences.en: And I think it's the same when you go off.
sentences.zh: 我想当你停药时也是如此。

sentences.en: They call it the nocebo effect, which is if you think it's essential to you, you may be just afraid of stopping, afraid of finding out what that's like.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为反安慰剂效应，也就是说如果你认为它对你至关重要，你可能只是害怕停药，害怕去发现那种感觉是什么样的。

sentences.en: And that could sort of contribute to your feeling bad.
sentences.zh: 而这可能会导致你感觉糟糕。

sentences.en: Michael, in your case, what did you conclude about stopping?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，就你而言，你对停药得出了什么结论？

sentences.en: Me, I don't know that I've ever gotten far enough along in the conversation with myself to stop.
sentences.zh: 我嘛，我不知道自己是否曾在内心的对话中走到过考虑停药这一步。

sentences.en: I just know that on the occasions when I have failed to reliably take Lexapro, I have experienced some really crippling headaches,
sentences.zh: 我只知道，每当我没有按时可靠地服用来士普时，我就会经历一些非常剧烈的头痛，

sentences.en: which I needed a doctor to tell me were from not taking my Lexapro reliably.
sentences.zh: 这些头痛需要医生告诉我，是因为我没有规律服用来士普导致的。

sentences.en: But there was no deeper conversation.
sentences.zh: 但并没有更深入的对话。

sentences.en: There was no, is it time to think about whether you should be tapering?
sentences.zh: 没有问：是时候考虑你是否应该减量了吗？

sentences.en: How long have you been on it?
sentences.zh: 你吃了多久了？

sentences.en: It was just an accepted fact in my conversation with the doctor that I was on it, and then I'd probably still be on it for as long as I'm going to be on it.
sentences.zh: 在我与医生的对话中，这是一个已被接受的事实：我在吃药，而且我可能只要该吃就会一直吃下去。

sentences.en: And do you think that that conversation should have happened when you first went on?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种对话应该在你刚开始吃药的时候就进行吗？

sentences.en: I wonder now.
sentences.zh: 我现在开始琢磨了。

sentences.en: But now I'm asking myself the question of are we all infantilizing ourselves in the face of medicine?
sentences.zh: 但现在我正在问自己一个问题：在医学面前，我们是不是都在把自己变得像小孩子一样无知？

sentences.en: And should I be asking this question myself?
sentences.zh: 我是不是应该自己来问这个问题？

sentences.en: Why should I be waiting for a doctor to ask it?
sentences.zh: 为什么我要等医生来问？

sentences.en: It's getting a little existential now.
sentences.zh: 现在这变得有点存在主义的意味了。

sentences.en: I mean, some people have multiple remissions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人会多次缓解。

sentences.en: And what I hear from physicians is if you've had like three episodes of depression, then you probably are going to take an SSRI for indefinitely as a maintenance treatment.
sentences.zh: 我从内科医生那里听到的是，如果你有过大约三次抑郁发作，那你大概作为维持治疗需要无限期地服用SSRIs（选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂）。

sentences.en: And if it's fewer than three, then no, then you should try to get off if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果少于三次，那就不用，如果你想的话，你应该尝试停药。

sentences.en: But I don't think there's a lot of energy around having that conversation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为大家并没有花太多精力去进行这种对话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking about deprescription here because that's the conversation that RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在这里谈论减药，是因为这是小肯尼迪

sentences.en: and those around him want us to be having.
sentences.zh: 以及他身边的人希望我们进行的那种对话。

sentences.en: But there's also a possibility that people are going to hear this conversation and instead of just deprescription, they're going to hear maybe I shouldn't ever get a prescription.
sentences.zh: 但也有这样一种可能，人们听到这个对话后，想到的可能不仅仅是减药，而是觉得自己也许根本就不应该开处方药。

sentences.en: And I wonder if that's a risk that RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否是小肯尼迪

sentences.en: and the medical experts who are now joining him in this conversation are thinking about.
sentences.zh: 以及现在加入他探讨这个话题的医学专家们正在考虑的风险。

sentences.en: I mean, because I cover psychiatry and mental health, I have been doing interviews all over the country about people's use of this kind of medication.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，由于我主要负责精神病学和心理健康的报道，我一直在全国各地就人们使用这类药物的情况进行采访。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you that like they're reaching parts of society that just wouldn't have gotten any kind of mental health care in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须告诉你，这些药物正在触及社会上那些过去根本无法获得任何心理健康护理的群体。

sentences.en: So I remember talking to I think he was an auto mechanic and I was doing interviews in a school parking lot.
sentences.zh: 我记得我和一个汽车修理工交谈过，当时我正在一所学校的停车场进行采访。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, like my father was an angry drunk.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，就像我父亲以前是个脾气暴躁的酒鬼一样。

sentences.en: And because I take an antidepressant, I know I'm not going to go that way.
sentences.zh: 而因为我服用了抗抑郁药，我知道自己不会走上那条老路。

sentences.en: And there are groups within our society that are only now for the first time getting access to a treatment for depression or a treatment for anxiety.
sentences.zh: 在我们社会中，有些群体直到现在才第一次获得治疗抑郁症或焦虑症的机会。

sentences.en: I mean, I think if you look at the numbers, white people take antidepressants at a rate that is twice as high as any other racial category.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看一下数据，白人服用抗抑郁药的比例是任何其他种族群体的两倍。

sentences.en: And like five times as high as Asian people.
sentences.zh: 几乎是亚裔的五倍。

sentences.en: So there's just a huge discrepancy.
sentences.zh: 所以这里存在着巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Some groups take these a lot.
sentences.zh: 有些群体大量使用这些药物。

sentences.en: Some groups really don't have much access.
sentences.zh: 而有些群体则几乎没有什么获取途径。

sentences.en: In other words, because of the demographics of who takes these mental health drugs,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，由于服用这些精神健康药物的人口统计学特征，

sentences.en: there are plenty of people who perhaps could benefit from them who have never been introduced to them or are just starting culturally to accept the idea that they can and will be on them.
sentences.zh: 有大量本可以从中受益的人，要么从未接触过它们，要么才刚刚从文化上接受他们可以并且将会服用这些药物的观念。

sentences.en: And the overprescription, deprescription conversation isn't necessarily the right one for them to be having right now.
sentences.zh: 关于过度开药和减少用药的讨论，对他们来说现在未必是合适的时机。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样的。

sentences.en: I mean, it may be that there is no one message that is appropriate for our entire society.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能并没有一种信息适用于我们整个社会。

sentences.en: So I think RFK Jr., the secretary,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为被提名为部长的RFK Jr.，

sentences.en: has to be very careful about encouraging this conversation about stopping medication when it's appropriate without driving people away from the idea of treatment completely.
sentences.zh: 在鼓励讨论适时停药时必须非常小心，以免把人们完全吓得不敢接受治疗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's one thing to have a conversation about deprescription.
sentences.zh: 探讨减少用药是一回事。

sentences.en: It's another to intentionally or not stigmatize ever getting a prescription.
sentences.zh: 而有意或无意地给任何处方药的使用贴上污名化标签则是另一回事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think both of these conversations need to happen.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这两种对话都需要进行。

sentences.en: How to access treatment that people really desperately need and also how much is enough and how to stop.
sentences.zh: 一方面是如何获得人们迫切需要的治疗，另一方面是多少才算够以及如何停药。

sentences.en: Well, Ellen, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，埃伦，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此表示感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: As a new round of peace talk started between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周日，随着美国与伊朗新一轮和平谈判的开始，以色列与黎巴嫩真主党之间的冲突给谈判蒙上了阴影。

sentences.en: and Iran on Sunday, the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon threw a wrench into the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 以色列与真主党之间的交火促使伊朗宣称其将再次关闭霍尔木兹海峡，不过美国官员表示该威胁并未付诸实施。

sentences.en: Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah prompted Iran to claim it was once again closing the Strait of Hormuz, a threat U.S.
sentences.zh: 伊朗要求黎巴嫩的战事立即停止，但在过去几周里，那里的停火协议屡次宣布、屡次破裂又屡次恢复。

sentences.en: officials said had not been carried out.
sentences.zh: 官员表示该威胁并未付诸实施。

sentences.en: Iran has demanded that fighting in Lebanon end immediately, but ceasefires there have been declared, broken, and reinstated several times over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 伊朗要求黎巴嫩的战事立即停止，但在过去几周里，那里的停火协议屡次宣布、屡次破裂又屡次恢复。

sentences.en: And problems with President Trump's $14 million renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, time for America's 250th birthday next month,
sentences.zh: 而特朗普总统为迎接下个月美国建国250周年而对林肯纪念堂倒影池进行的1400万美元的翻新工程出现了种种问题，

sentences.en: have become so severe that Trump said he will have to partially drain the pool for repairs.
sentences.zh: 严重到特朗普表示他不得不部分排干水池以进行维修。

sentences.en: Over the past few days, the pool's new coat of dark blue paint, applied by a company that has never before worked for the federal government, has begun to visibly peel,
sentences.zh: 在过去的几天里，水池刷上的新的深蓝色涂料开始出现肉眼可见的剥落，这些涂料是由一家从未为联邦政府工作过的公司涂刷的，

sentences.en: and green algae has spread across the pool, likely because the renovation project does not fix the pool's malfunctioning filtration system.
sentences.zh: 并且水池中已经滋生了绿藻，这很可能是因为该翻新工程并没有修复水池失灵的过滤系统。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: I'm sorry!
sentences.zh: 对不起！

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了自称是改革派的一群人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时甚至令人兴奋的权力争斗中。

sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失控的故事。
